metaDescription: SPT countertop dishwashers compared across the SD-2224 and SD-2225 families: cycles, delay start, dispenser, Energy Star and which model suits your kitchen.
expertTake: The SD-2225DWA is the best overall SPT because it states six place settings and a low 17.24 inch height. The SD-2224DW is the value pick for its seven cycles and stainless interior. Anyone without a threaded faucet should skip SPT, since every model here is faucet-fed.
introParagraphs: One maker's lineup can look like a wall of model numbers, with the same machine sold in white and silver under different suffixes. Sorting them by family is the only way to see what really changes between them.

Every unit in this guide is a faucet-fed machine with delay start and an efficiency rating. They differ in cycle lists, dispenser hardware and the details of the control panel, so the buying question is which family fits how you cook and load, and whether your faucet and cabinet can host it at all.

products.name: SPT SD-2225DWA Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Settings, LED
products.description:
The SD-2225DWA is the SPT that states its capacity plainly: up to six standard place settings and dishware up to 10.25 inches in diameter. At only 17.24 inches tall it clears most wall cabinets, and the maker pitches it at apartments, office kitchens and other small spaces. Delay start, an LED display and an Energy Star rating complete a full-size style feature set.

Against the SD-2224DW below it has fewer stated cycles in the available text, so check the manual for the program list before you rely on a particular mode. What you gain is a clearer capacity claim and a low profile. The 10.25 inch plate limit is the main constraint, since many modern dinner plates are bigger.

Ownership is the faucet-fed routine: attach the hose, load, run and drain. Leave the hose attached when the machine lives beside the sink, and rinse the filter every few loads. A level counter keeps noise down.
products.bestFor: Apartment and office kitchens that need a stated six-setting capacity in a low body.
pros: Six standard place settings stated plainly
Low 17.24 inch height fits under most cabinets
cons: Plate limit of 10.25 inches excludes large plates
Program list is not detailed in the listing

products.name: SPT SD-2224DW Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher, 7 Cycles

specList.label: Cycles
specList.value: Heavy, normal, light, mini party, rinse, speed, soak

specList.label: Connection
specList.value: Universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect

products.description:
The SD-2224DW is the SPT with the longest cycle list and the most distinctive extras. Seven cycles include Heavy, normal, light, mini party, rinse, speed and soak, and a delay start can be set to two, four, six or eight hours. A stainless steel interior resists staining and odor better than plastic, which matters for a machine that sits between loads.

The mini party cycle is the unusual entry, aimed at a small batch of glasses and plates after a gathering, while soak softens dried food before a wash. A universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect handle the hookup. Compared with the SD-2225DWA it gives you more cycle choice but a vaguer capacity claim in the listing text.

In ownership the stainless interior is the long-term benefit. It cleans easily, holds less smell and will not discolor like a plastic tub. Use soak for baked-on food, keep the filter clean and wipe the seal weekly, and use mini party only for a small batch of glasses and plates so the chamber is not wasted on a nearly empty rack.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a stainless interior and a wide cycle list.
pros: Seven cycles including soak and mini party
Delay start in 2, 4, 6 or 8 hour steps
Stainless steel interior resists stains and odor
Universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect
cons: Capacity is not stated in the available text
More cycles than most people will use

products.name: SPT SD-2224DSB Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher, LED, Dispenser
products.description:
The SD-2224DSB adds hardware the others lack: an automatic detergent and rinse agent dispenser. Instead of dropping a tablet into the chamber, you fill the dispensers and the machine releases the right amount at the right moment, which is how full-size dishwashers work. Electronic controls with an LED display, delay start and Energy Star certification fill out the package.

The automatic rinse agent dispenser is the practical benefit. Rinse aid reduces spotting and helps dishes dry, which is the weak point of small washers. Against the SD-2225DWA it adds the dispenser but states less about capacity and height in the available text.

Use the dispenser as designed, with dishwasher detergent only and rinse agent in its own reservoir, and keep both topped up so a load never runs dry. Refill as the manual says, rinse the filter regularly and check the hose connection every few months.
products.bestFor: Households that want rinse aid and detergent handled automatically.
pros: Automatic detergent and rinse agent dispenser
cons: Capacity and height are not stated in the listing text

products.name: SPT SD-2225DS Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Cycles, Glass and ECO

specList.label: Cycles
specList.value: Heavy, normal, ECO, Glass, Speed, Rinse

specList.label: Connection

products.description:
The SD-2225DS carries a leaner cycle list than the SD-2224DW but swaps in two useful entries: ECO and Glass. The six cycles are Heavy, normal, ECO, Glass, Speed and Rinse, with delay start in two, four, six or eight hour steps. A Glass cycle is a real benefit for anyone who washes stemware and tumblers, since a gentler program protects thin glass.

The ECO setting trades heat and time for lower energy use, a fair choice for lightly soiled loads. Universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect handle the hookup, and the Energy Star rating supports the efficiency claim. Compared with the 7-cycle SD-2224DW it lacks soak and mini party, but it adds Glass and ECO.

The silver finish suits stainless kitchens. Ownership is the standard faucet-fed routine, with a filter rinse every few loads and a monthly hot cycle. The same cycle list is sold in white under a sibling suffix, so choose the finish that fits your kitchen.
products.bestFor: Kitchens that wash a lot of glassware and want an ECO option.

ECO cycle for lightly soiled loads

Universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect
cons: No soak or mini party cycle
Capacity is not stated in the listing text

buyingCriteria.criterion: Cycle list and what it does
buyingCriteria.explanation: The SD-2224 family lists seven cycles: Heavy, normal, light, mini party, rinse, speed and soak. The SD-2225DS lists six: Heavy, normal, ECO, Glass, Speed and Rinse. Soak and Glass are the two that change results, because soak softens dried food and Glass protects thin stemware. Pick the family whose special cycle you will use. A common mistake is to pay for a long cycle list and then run Normal every night. Think about the dishes you actually wash: if you rarely leave plates to dry, soak adds little, and if you own no stemware, Glass adds nothing. Choose the list that matches your habits, not the longest list.

Only the SD-2225DWA states six standard place settings and dishware up to 10.25 inches, with a height of 17.24 inches. Other SPT listings give less. A machine that states its limits is easier to fit to your kitchen. Measure the gap under your cabinet before buying any of them. Plate size is the quiet constraint, because a 10.25 inch limit rules out many modern dinner plates, which run 10.5 to 11 inches. Salad plates, bowls and mugs fit easily, so households with oversized plates should confirm the fit or handwash those few pieces.

Delay start lets you load after dinner and run the machine later. The SD-2224 and SD-2225 families offer steps of two, four, six or eight hours. That is useful for off-peak power rates and for quiet evenings. Make sure you will actually use it, since a timer you ignore adds nothing. The timer also solves a noise problem, because the pump and the drain phase run while you sleep or work elsewhere. If your electricity plan has cheaper off-peak hours, a delayed start can shift the heating load to the lower rate without any effort from you.

The SD-2224DSB has an automatic detergent and rinse agent dispenser, which is rare in a countertop machine. Rinse aid reduces spots and helps drying, which are the weak points of small washers. A dispenser adds a refill routine, and it only pays off if you use rinse aid regularly. Fill the rinse reservoir only to the line, because overfilling leaves streaks and suds. If you prefer all-in-one tablets, check the manual first, since some small machines dislike them and a dispenser can clog with a tablet that did not dissolve.

The SD-2224DW lists a stainless steel interior. Stainless resists staining, holds less odor and lasts longer than plastic in a machine that sits between loads. Plastic tubs are cheaper and work fine, but they discolor with tomato sauce and turmeric. Check which interior the model you choose has. Stainless also tolerates hot cycles and dishwasher cleaner better over the years, and it does not trap smells from garlic or curry. If a model does not list its interior material, assume plastic and plan to run a cleaning cycle more often.

Every SPT in this guide is faucet-fed, with a universal faucet adapter and Quick Connect on several. That works with standard threaded spouts and fails on pull-out sprayers and some designer faucets. Unscrew the aerator and check for threads before ordering. If your faucet does not fit, choose a tank model from another maker. Renters should also check the lease, because attaching and detaching a hose over a long period can wear a faucet. A leaking connection under a cabinet damages wood slowly, so look at the fitting each month with a dry towel.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cycle value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the cycle lists and asked which entries change results. Soak and Glass counted, while overlapping speed modes did not. The SD-2224DW and SD-2225DS earned credit for different reasons. We also looked at whether the list is easy to read, because a panel with seven cycles and an LED display needs clear labels. Cycles that do the same job under different names counted once.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated limits
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded listings that state capacity, plate size and height. The SD-2225DWA was the only SPT to state all three, so it scored highest for fit clarity. A listing that tells you the plate limit and the height saves you from a return, and we treated that kind of honesty as a feature. Listings that give only a weight or a country of origin gave us nothing to score. Two SPT listings fell into that group, which is why we ranked by the model families rather than by every suffix on offer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hardware extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted the stainless interior on the SD-2224DW and the dispenser on the SD-2224DSB as real hardware advantages. Extra hardware earns credit only when owners will use it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Faucet hookup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the universal adapter and Quick Connect, noting that every model depends on a compatible faucet. That dependence is the family's main limitation.

howWeEvaluated.title: Variant clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: SPT sells many suffixes, including white and silver versions of the same cycle list. Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, we grouped them by family and said where a finish choice is the only difference.

cards.label: SD-2224 family
cards.text: The SD-2224DW lists seven cycles and a stainless interior, and the SD-2224DSB adds a dispenser. This family is about hardware and cycle choice.

cards.label: SD-2225 family
cards.text: The SD-2225DWA states six place settings and a 17.24 inch height, and the SD-2225DS adds Glass and ECO cycles. This family is about stated capacity and a low body.

howToChoose.note: Pick by features, not by finish or suffix. Choose the 2224 line for hardware and the 2225 line for clear fit and glassware. Within each line the white and silver versions share a cycle list, so pick the finish that matches your appliances. If a listing is vague, read the full bullet list, because the features, not the model letters, decide what you are buying.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A stated height, a plate limit that matches your dinnerware and a faucet that takes the adapter. Confirm the delay start steps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SD-2225DWA is the clearest fit because it states six settings, a 10.25 inch plate limit and a 17.24 inch height.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want the stainless interior and the soak cycle of the SD-2224DW, or the glass and ECO cycles of the SD-2225DS.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a stated six-setting machine with a timer. The SD-2225DWA covers that at the lowest position here.

maintenance.why: Debris clogs the screen and weakens spray. A clean filter keeps results consistent. Twist it out, rinse under running water and brush off film with a soft brush before seating it again.

faq.q: Which SPT has the most cycles?
faq.a: The SD-2224DW lists seven: Heavy, normal, light, mini party, rinse, speed and soak. The SD-2225DS lists six, with Glass and ECO in place of soak and mini party.

faq.q: Are the white and silver versions different?
faq.a: Often only in finish, but check the listing. SPT sells the same cycle list under different suffixes, so compare features rather than model letters. Read the bullet list on each listing and confirm the cycle names, the delay start steps and the interior material. If two listings list the same features, the finish is the only real difference.

faq.q: Do SPT dishwashers work without a faucet?
faq.a: No. The models in this guide are faucet-fed. If your faucet has no thread, choose a tank model from another maker. Several makers sell machines with a built-in tank that need only a power outlet and a drain hose, which suits renters and campers better than a faucet-fed unit.

faq.q: What is the delay start for?
faq.a: It postpones the wash by two, four, six or eight hours on the families listed here. Use it to run overnight or during off-peak power hours. Load the machine, set the delay and leave the hose connected, so nothing needs your attention until the cycle has finished and the chamber has cooled.

faq.q: Is the stainless interior worth it?
faq.a: For long-term ownership, yes. It resists staining and holds less odor than plastic, and it cleans easily. If you cook a lot of tomato sauce or curry, a plastic tub can discolor over a year, and the stainless interior avoids that.

faq.q: Will it fit large dinner plates?
faq.a: The SD-2225DWA lists dishware up to 10.25 inches, so larger plates may not fit. Measure your plates before buying any SPT. Bowls, mugs and salad plates fit easily, and many owners simply handwash the few oversized plates and run everything else through the machine.
